vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes reach every dependency, not just the toolkit. Renovate injects this object as a `force` block on the vulnerable dep, and force outranks packageRules, so the dashboard-approval rule below cannot hold a security PR back. dependencyDashboardApproval is repeated here on purpose: force carries only the keys written in this object, so without it the rule below would still apply and a security PR would sit waiting for a tick. Dependabot's own automated security fixes are deliberately left disabled so only one bot opens security PRs.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Weekly refresh of pnpm-lock.yaml to the newest in-range versions. This is the only mechanism here that reaches transitive dependencies: a version PR bumps declared ranges and a security PR needs a fixed version it is allowed to select, but neither moves a transitive dep whose parent range already permits the fixed version. That is the class of alert that accumulates otherwise.

packageRules.description: Everything outside the toolkit is listed on the Dependency Dashboard and opens a PR only when ticked there. This replaces a blanket `enabled: false`, which suppressed the lookup entirely and left non-toolkit dependencies invisible rather than merely unautomated.

GitHub Actions skip the dashboard tick and open PRs directly. The dashboard is the right default for npm, where a tick costs one click against hundreds of dependencies, but there are only nine actions here and seven of them float on a major tag (`@v7`), which Renovate re-resolves in place - so for those it proposes majors and nothing else. A major of a release-critical action is the exact failure this repo already had: @changesets/cli v3 needed changesets/action@v2, the workflow stayed on v1, and three releases cut tags while publishing no image. That update must arrive as a reviewable PR, not as a line on a dashboard nobody reads. Deliberately no automerge: majors are the only thing this manager will mostly produce, and majors are what broke it.

toolkit-hub packages are released together and consumed only through the pnpm catalog, so they travel as a single PR, and they are the one group that does not wait for a dashboard tick. rangeStrategy 'bump' is what makes the catalog track releases at all: under the default 'replace' an in-range release (^0.5.7 -> 0.5.8) would change only pnpm-lock.yaml and the catalog entry would silently drift behind. registryUrls is not redundant with the root .npmrc: Renovate attaches a package file's .npmrc to package.json files only, so catalog entries in pnpm-workspace.yaml would otherwise be looked up on registry.npmjs.org and every one of them would 404.

Patch and minor merge themselves once the workspace verify job is green. Majors always wait for a human. platformAutomerge is off above because the repo has allow_auto_merge disabled and no branch protection, so Renovate must check the branch status itself rather than hand the merge to GitHub.

Container base images, and the hand-pinned `jq` Alpine package inside a RUN line, were invisible to Renovate before this: enabledManagers omitted `dockerfile` entirely, and no manager at all reads a version pinned inside a RUN line. Two of the four tracked base images are security-relevant - gcr.io/distroless/nodejs24-debian12 trails node:24-trixie-slim's own Node patch level, so this is the only automated path a Node security patch has into the distroless runtime image. `custom.regex` covers the `jq=1.8.2-r0` pin via the `apk` datasource - not `alpine_3_xx`, which does not exist anywhere in Renovate's source or docs; `apk` is the real one, confirmed against lib/modules/datasource/apk/readme.md upstream. Its registryUrlTemplate branch (v3.23) was read off the actual pulled image (`docker run nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.29-alpine cat /etc/os-release`) and cross-checked against the live Alpine v3.23 APKINDEX, which lists jq 1.8.2-r0 in `main` - matching the current pin exactly. That branch is a hand-maintained fact, not something Renovate infers: if nginx-unprivileged's own Alpine base ever moves to a newer release, this config keeps pointing at v3.23 and keeps proposing valid-but-increasingly-stale v3.23 updates rather than erroring - the same quiet-drift failure shape as an unset registryUrls above, not a loud one. gcr.io needed no registryUrls/hostRules of its own: distroless is a public repo and Renovate's docker datasource reaches it with the same anonymous bearer-token flow every public v2 registry supports, confirmed directly against gcr.io's token endpoint. Bypasses the dashboard tick like github-actions above: five pins total (four images plus jq) do not need a per-tick approval, and the two security-relevant images should surface as PRs on their own, not sit unticked. Deliberately no automerge and no groupName, unlike toolkit-hub: a Dockerfile-only change matches neither `.github/paths-filter-deps.yaml` nor any app's entry in `.github/paths-filter-apps.yaml` (both are keyed to package/app subtrees; the shared root Dockerfile is in neither), so today such a change runs only hadolint - never a docker build, never the app test suite that gates the toolkit-hub automerge above. A base-image bump ships straight to production through the release pipeline, and this Dockerfile leans hard on exact base-image internals (distroless's node-as-ENTRYPOINT argv convention, numeric USER 65532/101) that AGENTS.md documents as load-bearing and a new tag could change without notice - every one of these waits for a human. Each image is also a different vendor on its own release cadence, so grouping them would make a bad one harder to isolate and revert; the two `node:24-alpine` config-validator stages already collapse into one PR under Renovate's default per-dependency grouping, with no groupName needed for that.

customManagers.description: Targets the `jq=1.8.2-r0` pin in the two nginx-unprivileged UI stages - see the packageRules entry above for the datasource choice and the registryUrlTemplate branch's provenance.
